glosses: The part of Earth which is not covered by oceans or other bodies of water.

examples.text: Most insects live on land.

glosses: Real estate or landed property; a partitioned and measurable area which is owned and acquired and on which buildings and structures can be built and erected.

examples.text: There are 50 acres of land in this estate.

glosses: A country or region.

examples.text: They come from a faraway land.

glosses: A person's country of origin and/or homeplace; homeland.
The soil, in respect to its nature or quality for farming.

examples.text: wet land
good or bad land for growing potatoes

glosses: Realm, domain.

examples.text: I'm going to Disneyland.
Maybe that's how it works in TV-land, but not in the real world.

glosses: The ground left unploughed between furrows.
Any of several portions into which a field is divided for ploughing.
A shock or fright.

examples.text: He got an awful land when the police arrived.

glosses: A conducting area on a board or chip which can be used for connecting wires.
On a compact disc or similar recording medium, an area of the medium which does not have pits.

examples.text: Now, assume that the recording is being done with 100 grooves per inch, and that the record groove is .006 inch wide. This means that the land on either side on any given groove in the absence of sound waves is .004 inch.

glosses: The non-airline portion of an itinerary. Hotel, tours, cruises, etc.

examples.text: Our city offices sell a lot more land than our suburban offices.

glosses: The lap of the strakes in a clinker-built boat; the lap of plates in an iron vessel; called also landing.
In any surface prepared with indentations, perforations, or grooves, that part of the surface which is not so treated, such as the level part of a millstone between the furrows.
In any surface prepared with indentations, perforations, or grooves, that part of the surface which is not so treated, such as the level part of a millstone between the furrows.
The space between the rifling grooves in a gun.

examples.text: The FBI maintains a database, the General Rifling Characteristics (GRC) file, which is organized by caliber, number of lands and grooves, direction of twist, and width of lands and grooves, to help an examiner figure out the origin of a recovered bullet.
The human eye is a precision instrument. It can detect grooves and lands on a slug more efficiently than any computer.

glosses: A group of dwellings or tenements under one roof and having a common entry.
To descend to a surface, especially from the air.

examples.text: The plane is about to land.

glosses: To alight, to descend from a vehicle.

examples.text: 10. You will be civil and attentive to passengers, giving proper assistance to ladies and children getting in or out, and never start the car before passengers are fairly received or landed.

glosses: To come into rest.
To arrive on land, especially a shore or dock, from a body of water.

examples.text: Tatan and Erhtan are two small islands in the sea southwest of Kinmen.[…]A contingent of some 30 Communist troops tried to land at Erhtan, but were disarmed by Government defenders.

glosses: To bring to land.

examples.text: It can be tricky to land a helicopter.
Use the net to land the fish.
I'll undertake to land them on our coast.

glosses: To capture or arrest.

examples.text: `He told me that he was certain that Coates shot at him. We threw out a drag and landed Coates within an hour.'

glosses: To acquire; to secure.

examples.text: She landed a job at the company.
As Di Matteo celebrated and captain John Terry raised the trophy for the fourth time, the Italian increased his claims to become the permanent successor to Andre Villas-Boas by landing a trophy.
Siemens has landed a contract to upgrade signalling on the entire 170km (105-mile) S-Bane suburban network in Copenhagen to pave the way for fully automated trains.

glosses: To succeed in having sexual relations with; to score.

examples.text: Too ugly to ever land a chick.

glosses: To deliver.

examples.text: If you land a knockout blow, you’ll win the match.

glosses: To connect (to arrive at an intended target).

examples.text: If the punches land, you might lose a few teeth!

Vice President J. D. Vance has lashed out at [Gavin] Newsom, telling Fox that the Californian’s attacks aren’t landing, because his trolling “ignores the fundamental genius of President Trump’s political success, which is that he’s authentic”; […].

glosses: To go down well with an audience.

examples.text: Some of the comedian's jokes failed to land.
We told an Amelia Earhart joke yesterday—did not go great with the audience. Someone wrote: "You can't be surprised when an Amelia Earhart joke doesn't land."

glosses: lant; urine
To bring to a conclusion.

examples.text: The band usually ends up their concerts with their biggest hit song.

glosses: To come to a final place, condition, or situation, sometimes unplanned or unexpected; to turn out.

examples.text: They ended up angry at each other.
He ended up as an insurance agent.
I was going for a stroll, and ended up lost.
She gave her all, and ended up winning the contest.

glosses: To lift or tilt, so as to set on end.

examples.text: to end up a hogshead

glosses: Arriver au voisinage de la terre.

examples.text: Si l'un des pèlerins venait à mourir sur le bateau, le capitaine devrait ne point pratiquer aussitôt l’immersion, mais bien atterrir quelque part et faire ensevelir le défunt dans un cimetière.
Pendant la saison d’été, les navires de la Compagnie pourraient donc facilement atterrir au cap Bathurst par la voie du nord-ouest.
En 1905, la « Belgica » atterrit par 76°37’ soit à deux degrés plus au Nord qu’aucun autre navire.
Le vendredi 13 mars, j’aurais dû apercevoir dans la soirée le feu de Sombrero, sur lequel je voulais atterrir […].

glosses: Reprendre contact avec le sol.

examples.text: D'autre part, Wynmalen a dû s'arrêter à Launois-sur-Vence pour être ravitaillé, puis dut atterrir de nouveau à Montigny sur route, à dix kilomètres de Metz. Il ne repartira que ce matin.

Brusquement je m’aperçois que le terrain est en pente et que, si j’atterris dans la longueur, je risque d’avoir une roue plus bas que l’autre et d’être entraîné dans un « cheval de bois » dont on ne sait d’avance les fantaisies.

glosses: Parvenir dans un lieu déterminé.

examples.text: Comprenez que tous les macchabs, dès qu'ils sont assez légers pour descendre le courant – pas assez gonflés pour flotter –, qu'ils viennent de Bercy, de Charenton, de beaucoup plus loin, c'est ici même qu'ils « atterrissent ».
Comment avez-vous atterri ici? Puni? Il ne se passe jamais rien ici.

glosses: Tocar una embarcación con otra, o con un muelle o embarcadero.

examples.text: Hecha señal á la Triunfo, envió esta su jente armada, y unida á la de la Resolución bajo las órdenes del teniente de navío don Evaristo Casariego, abordaron el muelle, y sin resistencia de ninguna clase llegaron á la plaza.

glosses: En especial, abordar₁ con la intención de tomar por la fuerza.

examples.text: En esa época floreció más aún el contrabando entre españoles residentes en Nicaragua y Costa Rica con piratas y comerciantes Ingleses, Holandeses y Franceses, además desde el Realejo salían barcazas a abordar el Galeón que venía de Manila.

glosses: Entrar a una embarcación o, por extensión, a otro medio de transporte.

examples.text: Eran las dos y media de la mañana cuando Graciela, Andrés y yo, abordamos el tren en la estación de Newburg. Regresábamos en silencio, Graciela dormitando en el hombro de Andrés; él y yo, con la mirada sin mirar patinando en el cristal ónix del río.

glosses: Aproximarse a una persona o institución para hacer una pregunta, iniciar un diálogo o tratar un asunto.

examples.text: cuando por la noche abordó a su hijo, quedó estupefacto viendo que no negaba el crimen.
Abordar al destinatario por su nombre (si lo conoces) es preferible.

glosses: Por extensión, exponer y debatir un asunto.

examples.text: Sin embargo y de forma paradójica, la Unión abordó la cuestión agraria basándose fundamentalmente en las exigencias de jornaleros y arrendatarios.

glosses: Iniciar una tarea difícil.
